The store

The store is a sidecar git repository (default ~/thinkube-tandem-store), separate from your code: your thinking never pollutes the project’s history, and the project never sees half-formed plans.

It is also the only thing that has to survive. Restore the store on a new machine and every space, every delivery and every record comes back — and re-attaches itself to the right repository, because the store carries the identity too. See Projects and identity.

What is in it

cards/<id>.yaml                 one project's identity: its minted id,
                                its labels, and how to find the
                                repository it belongs to
spaces/<project-id>/            every thinking space of one project
  <space-name>/
    name.txt                    the space's name as you typed it
    <author>/
      runs/<TEP>.log            the run log, written as it happens
      runs/cut-<TEP>.json       the signed cut
      deliveries/<TEP>.json     the delivery and its proofs
      digests/<ask>.md          the cited context digest per ask
      graphs/                   the derived graph
      records/                  the space's history, snapshot by snapshot
  tep-counter-<author>.txt      the author's TEP numbering
products/<name>.yaml            a product grouping label
defects/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl         the defect ledger — see below
headless/                       runs started from the command line

The defect ledger lives at the root

defects/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl sits at the store’s root, not inside a space. Every space writes to the same monthly file and every row names the space it came from.

That placement is deliberate: the ledger is how the methodology learns, and deleting a space must never delete the evidence of what went wrong in it. A row outlives its space.

Three disciplines guard it

  • Autosync. The store commits and pushes itself every five minutes when dirty — the pushed remote is the backup. A stale git lock left by a dead process is detected and cleared rather than failing every sync after it.

  • Secret scan. Every write is scanned for secret-shaped content (tokens, keys, private key blocks); a hit refuses the write and names the pattern. Nothing secret-shaped reaches disk.

  • Verbatim asks. Your words are stored as typed and never machine-edited.
